text: Why count operations rather than measure seconds?
choices: Counting is more accurate, since timing includes scheduling noise that cannot be removed.
Seconds vary between runs, while operation counts are constant for a given algorithm.
Operation counts include memory effects that a wall-clock measurement misses.
Counts are machine-independent and let you predict behavior at input sizes you have not run.
explanation: Twenty-four comparisons is twenty-four comparisons on any processor, in any language, in any decade. A timing cannot be extrapolated, because you do not know which effects are linear in n and which are not. Verified: searching ten million elements took 10,000,000 linear comparisons and 24 binary ones, and from those counts you can state what a billion elements costs without running anything.
